name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic (PVI D+6) with incumbent advantage
No polls or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Subramanyam: a D+6 district, incumbency, and a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge, while both Kalshi and Polymarket price his win odds at 95% or higher. With no contrary polling or ratings evidence, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger within single digits, or major outside spending against Subramanyam, would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term incumbent Suhas Subramanyam defends a Northern Virginia seat that leans Democratic by about six points, in a favorable national environment for his party. He has raised more than $1.1 million and holds over $580,000 on hand, supported by outside groups, while Republican Dave Beckwith has raised about $107,000. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity.

Prediction markets give Subramanyam a 95 to 97 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
